abstract: Freshwater resources are limited, and their availability is threatened by global climate change. Microalgae-based wastewater treatment enables water recovery for human activities, as microalgae can grow in wastewater while simultaneously removing contaminants within a circular economy framework. An example is OMWW. Thus, we tested the early and prolonged responses to tyrosol, p-coumaric acid, caffeic acid, their mixture and 10% OMWW on non-acclimated Dunaliella salina (Chlorophyta), analysing the effects through the DPPH and Comet assays. D. salina exhibited transient physiological damage after 1 day of exposure, whereas no detrimental effects were detected after 8 days, indicating the ability to withstand the toxicity of phenolic compounds and OMWW. Afterwards, we characterised the growth of acclimated D. salina cells to 10% OMWW at 100 and 300 mol photons m-2s-1, analysing the growth rate, pigment content, macromolecular composition and biomass reduction index. We observed that D. salina was able to grow similarly to the control in 10% OMWW when exposed to 300 mol photons m-2s-1, with a similar chla/chlb ratio and carotenoids, a higher amount of proteins and carbohydrates and a more reduced biomass. In conclusion, D. salina demonstrated a high degree of tolerance to OMWW and high acclimatation capability. Moreover, this study indicates that growth of D. salina in OMWW is strongly light-dependent.
